sentence: Não quero que sofram.
why: it follows “não quero que” (don't want … to), a wish that takes the subjunctive, and the English names the subject “them”, so it is eles.

sentence: Como se soletra?
why: with the impersonal “se” the verb is third-person singular, and “Como se soletra?” (how is it spelled) asks a general question, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: Solta a minha mão.
why: it is a direct command (Let go of my hand), and “solta” is the command form for tu, common in everyday Brazilian speech.

sentence: Solte o Tom.
why: it is a direct command telling the listener (“você”) to release Tom.

sentence: A ciência não soluciona todos os problemas da vida.
why: its subject is “A ciência” (science), and “não soluciona” (does not solve) states a general truth in the present indicative.

sentence: O todo é maior do que a soma das partes.
why: here “soma” is the noun “soma” (sum) in “a soma das partes” (the sum of the parts), not a form of the verb “somar”.

sentence: O vento sopra.
why: its subject is “O vento” (the wind), and the sentence states a general fact, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: Eu só sorri.
why: the subject is “eu”, and the English “I just smiled” reports a completed act in the past, so it is the preterite.

sentence: Não me subestime.
why: “Não me subestime” (don't underestimate me) is a direct negative command to “você”, and negative commands use this form.

sentence: Eu subi a cerca.
why: the subject is “eu”, and the English “I climbed” reports a completed act in the past.

sentence: Vamos ver o que se sucede.
why: its subject is “o que” (what), and the indirect question “o que se sucede” (what happens) uses the present indicative.

sentence: O vampiro suga meu sangue.
why: its subject is “O vampiro” (the vampire), and the English “is sucking” describes what is happening now, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: Só suma daqui!
why: it is a direct command telling the listener (“você”) to disappear (“suma daqui”, get out of here).

sentence: Ele supera todos os demais em seu trabalho.
why: the subject is “ele” (he), and it states a general fact in the present.

sentence: Suponhamos que ela esteja aqui.
why: it opens the sentence as an exhortation, “let's suppose”, a command that includes the speaker, nós.

sentence: Essa ponte não suporta caminhões pesados.
why: the subject is “essa ponte” (this bridge), and it states a lasting fact in the present.

sentence: Ela sustenta a família.
why: its subject is “Ela” (she), and “sustenta a família” (supports the family) describes an ongoing present situation, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: Se não quer ouvir, tape os ouvidos.
why: after “Se não quer ouvir” (if you don't want to listen), it tells that same listener, você, to cover “os ouvidos” (the ears), so it is the command.

sentence: Não temais, dizendo a verdade.
why: “Não temais” (fear not) is a direct negative command to “vós” (you all), and negative commands use this form.

sentence: O Tom não teme a morte.
why: its subject is “O Tom”, and “não teme” (doesn't fear) states a general fact, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: O Tom tem o que a Mary quer.
why: the subject is “o Tom”, and it states what he has now (“tem o que a Mary quer”, has what Mary wants).

sentence: Tem uma farmácia perto da minha casa.
why: impersonal “tem” (there is) has no subject and takes the third person singular, saying what exists near the house now.

sentence: Ela nunca toca nesse assunto.
why: its subject is “Ela” (she), and “nunca” (never) marks a habit, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: Falta de respeito não é algo que eu tolere facilmente.
why: it is in a relative clause after the negated “não é algo que” (is not something that), which takes the subjunctive, and its subject is “eu” (I).

sentence: Isso toma muito tempo.
why: the subject is “isso” (this), and it states a present fact (“toma muito tempo”, takes a lot of time).

sentence: Eu toparia uma cervejinha agora.
why: its subject is “Eu” (I), and it voices a hypothetical wish, the English “I wouldn't mind a beer”, so it is the conditional.

sentence: O que torna a América "América"?
why: its subject is “o que” (what), which takes the third person singular, and the question asks about the present.

sentence: Você vai ver o que é bom pra tosse!
why: here “tosse” is the noun “tosse” (cough) in the idiom “o que é bom pra tosse” (what's good for a cough), not a form of the verb “tossir”.

sentence: Onde é que Tom trabalha?
why: the subject is “Tom”, and the question asks where he works now, in the present.

sentence: Não fui eu que traduzi isso.
why: its subject is “eu” (I) in “fui eu que” (it was I who), and the English “translated” reports a completed act, so it is the preterite.

sentence: Eu não te traí.
why: the subject is “eu”, and the English “did not betray” denies a completed act in the past, so it is the preterite.

sentence: Eu não gostei da trama do filme.
why: here “trama” is the noun “trama” (plot) in “da trama do filme” (the movie's plot), not a form of the verb “tramar” (to weave).

sentence: O rádio transmite as notícias em detalhe.
why: its subject is “O rádio” (the radio), and the sentence describes what it regularly does, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: Por favor, transmita uma mensagem pra mim.
why: “Por favor, transmita uma mensagem” (please pass on a message) is a polite affirmative command to the listener, addressed as você.

sentence: O amor é um jogo em que sempre se trapaceia.
why: with the impersonal “se” (one) the verb is third-person singular, and “sempre” (always) marks a general truth, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: É disso que se trata.
why: in “se trata” (it is about) the verb is impersonal and takes the third person singular, and “é” (is) keeps it in the present.

sentence: Este sistema tem uma trava de segurança.
why: here “trava” is the noun “trava” (lock) after “uma” (a), not a form of the verb “travar” (to brake).

sentence: Traga o Tom para casa.
why: it opens the sentence as a direct command, telling the listener (“você”) to bring Tom home.

sentence: Apenas uma outra espécie de traça, a Antheraea mylitta, também produz fibra de seda.
why: here “traça” is the noun “traça” (moth) in “espécie de traça” (species of moth), not a form of the verb “traçar” (to make a stroke).

sentence: Trace uma linha reta.
why: “Trace uma linha reta” (draw a straight line) is an affirmative command to the listener, addressed as você.

sentence: Ele treinava para se tornar o melhor.
why: the subject is “ele” (he), and the imperfect describes a habit in the past (“used to train”).

sentence: Ele estava ao lado da treliça por onde trepava a fúcsia estimada dele.
why: its subject is “a fúcsia estimada dele” (his treasured fuchsia), placed after the verb, and it describes a past background scene with “estava”, so it is the imperfect.

sentence: Nós trocamos mensagens todos os dias.
why: its subject is “Nós” (we), and “todos os dias” (every day) marks a habit, so it is the present.

sentence: Dinheiro é a ultima coisa que ele quer.
why: here “ultima” is the adjective “última” (last), written without its accent, in “a ultima coisa” (the last thing), not a form of the verb “ultimar”.

sentence: Não ultrapasse o limite de velocidade.
why: “Não ultrapasse o limite” (don't exceed the limit) is a direct negative command to “você”, and negative commands use this form.

sentence: Eu tinha certeza de que você se uniria a nós.
why: its subject is “você”, which takes the third person singular, and after “tinha certeza de que” (was sure that) the conditional gives what was expected.

sentence: Ele utiliza bem seu tempo.
why: its subject is “Ele” (he), and “utiliza bem seu tempo” (makes good use of his time) describes his habit, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: Nós vagamos ao redor do centro de compras.
why: the subject is “Nós” (we), and the English “We wandered” reports a completed outing, so it is the preterite.

sentence: Eu achei que valeria a pena.
why: the English “it'd be worth it” shows the subject is a thing, third person singular, and after “achei que” (thought that) the conditional gives what was expected.

sentence: O ingresso vale por dois dias.
why: its subject is “O ingresso” (the ticket), and the sentence states a fact about it, so it is the present indicative.

sentence: Ele gritou "vaza!".
why: the shouted “vaza!” (get out) is a direct command, and informal Brazilian speech uses this tu imperative form for it.

sentence: Quem você quer que vença?
why: it follows “quer que” (want … to), a wish that takes the subjunctive, and its subject is “quem” (who), third person singular.

sentence: Nós vendemos tudo.
why: the subject is “nós” (we), and the English “we sell” states a general fact in the present.

sentence: Verifique de novo.
why: it is a direct command telling the listener (“você”) to check again (“de novo”).

sentence: Vigie a frente.
why: it is a direct command telling the listener (“você”) to watch the front.

sentence: Vira a página.
why: it is a direct command (Turn the page), and “vira” is the command form for tu, common in everyday Brazilian speech.

sentence: Voamos de Londres a Nova York.
why: no subject is named, the ending “-amos” is nós, and the English “we flew” reports a completed trip in the past, so it is the preterite.

sentence: Pode ser que voltem.
why: it follows “pode ser que” (it may be that), a possibility that takes the subjunctive, and the English gives the subject “they”.

sentence: Não se zangue.
why: it directly tells the listener not to get angry (“Não se zangue”), and a direct negative command to você uses this form.

sentence: Não zombe de mim!
why: “Não zombe de mim!” (don't make fun of me) is a direct negative command to “você”, and negative commands use this form.
